lane: MDC-88 (Marginal-Density Concentration), formerly proposed as KDMC-88
hypothesis_as_preregistered: KDMC-88: under alpha=0.2/beta=0.8 DTI with a 300 m triangular kernel the optimal binary field is a kernel-disjoint packing extended to every cell clearing the exact marginal bar, not a fixed ~37.6k-dot field at ~3 px spacing.
mechanism: exact DTI fractional-program algebra (marginal bar alpha*DTI*(1-k_self)/(1-alpha*DTI)) applied to a zero-catalogue PU density surface
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan wave-cut shoreline benches (~1,330 m) and alluvial-fan risers; GeoDAWN flight-line levelling seams in the magnetic bands. Both carried as explicit model features.
verdict_headline: The kernel-disjointness premise is falsified: tighter dot packing wins monotonically, because the official DTI charges false positives per DOT, not per unit of kernel area.
narrative: KDMC-88 preregistered that a >=6 px kernel-disjoint packing would beat the registry's ~3 px fields, on the argument that overlapping 300 m kernels pay for the same area twice. Reading vendor/gems57/metric.py line by line shows the false-positive term is FP_w = sum_x p(x)*(1 - k_self(x)): it is charged once per emitted dot and is completely independent of how much two dots' kernels overlap. Overlap costs nothing; only the dot count does. Because the true-positive term credits each truth pixel with the MAXIMUM kernel weight over all dots, and the truth is a set of one-pixel-wide lineaments, dots spaced 6 px apart leave the midpoints of a line uncovered (k(3)=0) while dots at 2.83 px keep every truth pixel within 1.41 px (k=0.53). The holdout confirms the algebra exactly: at a matched budget the score falls monotonically as separation grows, and the optimum sits at the tightest separation tested with roughly 1% of allowed cells emitted.

limitations: No organizer receipt exists for any file in this repository, so every figure here is HOLDOUT-DTI, PROXY or MODEL and none of them is a leaderboard score.
The holdout hides whole MAPPED fault components; the competition target is UNMAPPED faults. The holdout is the best available unbiased instrument, not the real task.

drivendata.org is unreachable from the build sandbox, so the public leaderboard value and the remaining weekly-slot balance cannot be verified here and are carried as UNVERIFIED human-supplied inputs.

metric.py's claim that the organizer masks mapped catalogue faults out of scoring traces to a forum thread that cannot be re-read from here; the candidate is built to be correct either way by emitting zero mass on mapped faults.

src/gems88/features.py cannot run on a clean checkout (IR-88-72): it requires acquisition_block_id_100m.tif and tiger_road_distance_m.tif, which exist in no pinned source. This lane therefore uses its own self-contained feature builder.
Two cores and 3 GB of RAM are available, so model capacity (250-iteration histogram gradient boosting) and the number of hide draws are compute-limited, not design-limited.

The blocked holdout CANNOT rank the catalogue-collar choice: every collar arm scores exactly 0.00000 there because the holdout's truth is withheld catalogue geometry. That question is answered only by the off-catalogue SGMC proxy, which is a PROXY.
